geometry_edits.rationale: Preserve the single dominant gesture while making the longitudinal body a little more legible and less box-like.
Reduce the bend slightly so the mass stays coherent across all views and does not over-fragment.
Add a real access-side court/void so the verified frontage becomes a legible public threshold.
Keep the void bounded and programmatic rather than turning the mass into a cut-up shell.
Orient the court toward the access side to satisfy the public-threshold requirement.
Make the new public void part of the root ancestry so the edited mass compiles as a single coherent program figure.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the dominant body by shifting the primary bar from a generic extrusion toward a slightly more articulated continuous mass.
Keep the dominant gesture aligned as a longitudinal bar so the mass remains readable in all four views.
Introduce a public void tied to the access edge to make the ground threshold more legible and programmatically active.
Keep the carve bounded so it reads as a usable court rather than a decorative bite.
Align the public opening to the program access side indicated in the brief.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass across views: a compact bar/plate with a mild bend and a stepped upper volume. The silhouette is not especially innovative, but it is resolved and not visually self-colliding. It fits neighborhood-living reasonably well because it can plausibly hold mixed-use floors above a street-active base. The main weakness is public-space articulation: the blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly, with no strong carved court, notch, or undercut that clearly welcomes the street. Sectionally it remains somewhat generic, but not contradictory to the brief. Overall, this is acceptable as an early massing diagram with a clear anchor, though it would benefit from a stronger access-side void.
